title: Unique lifting of factorizations across locally nilpotent ideals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $J\subseteq A$ a locally nilpotent ideal (every element of $J$ is nilpotent). For every monic polynomial $f\in A[T]$ and every factorization $\overline f=g_0h_0$ of its reduction $\overline f\in(A/J)[T]$ into monic polynomials $g_0,h_0\in(A/J)[T]$ generating the unit ideal of $(A/J)[T]$, there exist unique monic polynomials $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$ and reductions $\overline g=g_0$, $\overline h=h_0$ modulo $J$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ALI (lemma-locally-nilpotent-henselian), essential surjectivity of etale algebras and the final factorization paragraph

proof.text: For x in J and y in A, x*y lies in J and is nilpotent, so x*y+1 is a unit (IsNilpotent.isUnit_add_one). Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot gives J <= jacobson(bot). Thus isLocalHom_of_le_jacobson_bot makes the quotient map reflect units.

Use the simple-root definition of HenselianRing [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Given a monic P and x with P(x) in J and derivative a unit modulo J, the derivative is a unit in A by step 1. Choose n with P(x)^n=0. Mathlib.Dynamics.Newton, Polynomial.aeval_pow_two_pow_dvd_aeval_iterate_newtonMap, says P(x)^(2^n) divides P evaluated at the nth Newton iterate, hence that value is zero. Every iterate remains congruent to x modulo J: inductively the polynomial evaluation differs from P(x) by a multiple of the difference of the arguments (Polynomial.sub_dvd_eval_sub), so it belongs to J, and the next Newton correction is a multiple of this evaluation. This proves root lifting and hence HenselianRing A J.

Apply the proved henselianRing_iff_factorization_criterion [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion] to the HenselianRing A J proof from step 2. This gives monic g,h with f=g*h and prescribed reductions.

Coprimality lifts directly for nil ideals, without monicity or Nakayama. Given g,h-prime reducing to g0,h0, lift their Bezout coefficients to a,b in A[X] by Polynomial.map_surjective. The error a*g+b*h-prime-1 reduces to zero, so every coefficient lies in J and is nilpotent. Polynomial.isNilpotent_iff makes the error polynomial nilpotent; IsNilpotent.isUnit_add_one makes a*g+b*h-prime a unit. Multiply by its inverse and distribute to get IsCoprime g h-prime.

For another monic lift f=g-prime*h-prime, step 4 makes g,h-prime coprime. IsCoprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_right applied to g | g-prime*h-prime gives g | g-prime. In a subsingleton ring the pairs are equal immediately. Otherwise J is proper because 1 is not nilpotent, so A/J is nontrivial. Monic.natDegree_map and the equal reductions give equal degrees; Polynomial.eq_of_monic_of_dvd_of_natDegree_le gives g-prime=g. Finally Monic.isRegular cancels g to give h-prime=h, and Prod.ext gives equality of the pairs.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_monic_factorization_of_locally_nilpotent {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A) (hJ : ∀ x : A, x ∈ J → IsNilpotent x) (f : A[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (g₀ h₀ : (A ⧸ J)[X]) (hg₀ : g₀.Monic) (hh₀ : h₀.Monic) (hcoprime : IsCoprime g₀ h₀) (hfactor : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) = g₀ * h₀) : ∃! gh : A[X] × A[X], gh.1.Monic ∧ gh.2.Monic ∧ f = gh.1 * gh.2 ∧ gh.1.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) = g₀ ∧ gh.2.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) = h₀
